newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Qantas in compromise with airline.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Qantas in compromise with airline.

text.p: Qantas Airways Ltd said on Thursday that it would negotiate with start-up airline Aussie Airlines Pty Ltd with a view to entering into sub-leases at some of its terminals.

The proposed negotiations follow a settlement between Qantas and the Federal Airports Corp (FAC) after the FAC threatened to sue Qantas for allegedly breaching the terms of its leases by refusing to offer terminal space to Aussie Airlines.
The FAC will withdraw its notice that Qantas was in breach of its domestic terminal leases and Qantas will withdraw the application for an injunction against the FAC notice.

"Having regard to the outstanding Federal Court proceedings by Aussie Airlines against Qantas, all negotiations of the sub leases will be on the basis that all parties are reserving their rights, claims and defences in the proceedings," Qantas said.

Aussie Airlines is backed by Brian Grey, who started the original Compass Airlines, which was placed in liquidation in December 1991. Southern Cross Holdings Ltd carried on its airline business under the Compass banner until March 1993, but it was not associated with Grey.
Qantas is 25 percent owned by British Airways Plc.
